title: Verana Cross-Ecosystem Wallet Interop
description: Live trust-registry resolution wired into eight third-party identity wallets, replacing their hardcoded issuer lists.
longDescription: Every mature identity wallet ships a static list of trusted issuers, compiled at build time and updated by release. This work replaces that list with a live, fail-closed call to the Verana trust resolver, using the same HTTP surface in every target so the approach is portable rather than bespoke. Shipped and device-verified: MOSIP's Inji as a full issuer, wallet and verifier triangle; the EUDI reference Android wallet validated on testnet against France Identité's Unfold playground; Talao AltMe, Sphereon, Paradym and Procivis One built and demonstrated on device with both trusted and rogue paths verified; and Hologram running natively on vs-agent. SWIYU, the Swiss Confederation wallet, is partial: positive and control issuance flows are accepted on Android, one verifier request path remains blocked. Built for the Global Digital Trust Collaboration Award 2026, presenting at GDC Geneva in September 2026.

title: Credat
description: Trust layer for AI agents using DIDs and Verifiable Credentials.
longDescription: Credat is an open-source TypeScript library that brings decentralized identity to AI agent ecosystems. Agents get verifiable identities via did:web and did:key, issue scoped delegation credentials, and perform a cryptographic handshake to establish mutual trust. Built on W3C DID v1.1 and the Verifiable Credentials Data Model, with minimal dependencies and a transport-agnostic core. Around it sits a small suite: a CLI, drop-in protection for HTTP APIs, a LangChain and LangGraph integration, and runnable end-to-end demos.

title: Claw4S, Decentralized Agent Trust Protocol
description: Research paper and executable protocol for mutual cryptographic trust between AI agents, submitted to Stanford × Princeton hackathon.
longDescription: Submitted to the Claw4S Conference 2026 (Stanford × Princeton). A minimal protocol enabling two previously unknown AI agents to establish mutual cryptographic trust using did:key (Ed25519) and W3C Verifiable Credentials, without any central authority. The protocol completes in 2 round trips with under 2ms overhead and produces a fully auditable chain of signed credentials. Implemented as a single Python file with one dependency, featuring three execution modes (mock, live, attack) and a novel interactive lab format where the executing agent participates in the trust handshake.

title: Hologram Verifiable Service Agents
description: DIDComm and verifiable-credential AI agents running as production services on 2060.io's Hologram.
longDescription: Hologram is 2060.io's verifiable-trust messaging platform, where every connection between a human and an agent is gated by DIDs and verifiable credentials. I built and shipped several agents on it: a live-avatar agent backed by LiveKit that opens a session on connect, a multilingual concierge handling structured travel workflows, and a credential-gated automation bot. All are NestJS services deployed to Kubernetes with Helm, running on the vs-agent framework.

title: CiteMe
description: Generative engine optimization platform measuring how often AI search engines cite a brand.
longDescription: Search is moving from Google to AI answer engines. CiteMe crawls a site, runs multi-provider audits across the major AI engines, and returns a 0 to 100 score with prioritized, actionable fixes. A tracker surfaces real AI-bot visits so customers see which engines are reading their content. I co-founded it and serve as CIO, owning data, backend direction and infrastructure. Runs on Next.js 16, React 19, Supabase with pgvector for retrieval, a custom job queue, a multi-provider LLM layer, and Stripe billing.

title: Klyx
description: Web studio in Bordeaux building fast, design-led sites and web apps.
longDescription: Klyx is the web studio I founded in Bordeaux, run end to end: sales, design, development and delivery. Productized pricing runs from €900 one-pagers to €5,700+ custom builds, and client work ships with real payment and operations flows rather than brochureware. The studio also runs its own content engine, a Next.js and MDX blog at blog.klyx.fr with analytics, structured data and automated image pipelines.

title: Hop Hop Immo
description: Property-tech platform with a conversational AI agent over a catalogue of 30,000+ new-build listings.
longDescription: Hop Hop Immo is a property-tech platform building a virtual real-estate agent for new-build homes across France. I built Hoppy, a conversational AI assistant live in production that qualifies buyers and guides them to matching properties on demand, plus autonomous agents handling marketing automation. I also rebuilt the homepage with a targeted SEO architecture spanning 30+ city pages, 8 regions and a blog, and integrated the listing, CRM and analytics data flows that connect the 30,000+ property catalogue to the assistant.

title: Parkour Bassin d'Arcachon
description: Community website and member platform for the largest parkour club in southwestern France, co-founded in 2025.
longDescription: PKBA is the largest parkour club in southwestern France, which I co-founded and where I serve as treasurer and head of communication. Around 80 members today, growing to 110+ for the coming season. I designed and solo-built the club's production platform: a public site, online registration persisted to Airtable, an admin dashboard behind custom authentication to validate licences and export member data, and live Stripe flows for the merchandise shop and donations with automated receipts. I trained as a competitive parkour athlete from 2017 to 2025, so building this was as much a personal project as a technical one. The club has been featured by France 3 Nouvelle-Aquitaine.

title: VertiFlow
description: Parkour and urban-movement brand with a hand-built e-commerce storefront.
longDescription: VertiFlow is a parkour and urban-movement brand I founded, blending apparel, content and community to make the sport more accessible. I built and operate the entire storefront at vertiflow.fr from scratch: product catalogue, cart, checkout via serverless functions, promo codes and automated order emails, alongside the SEO blog, FAQ and full legal pages. Hand-coded and deployed on Netlify, and connected to the PKBA club ecosystem.

title: PkVision
description: Open-source computer vision for automatic parkour trick detection and scoring.
longDescription: PkVision applies pose estimation and movement classification to parkour footage, detecting tricks and scoring them automatically. It comes out of eight years in the sport and the judging problem that competitive parkour has never solved cleanly: scoring is subjective, and judges disagree. An open experiment at the intersection of the two things I spend my time on.

title: Reciproq
description: Marketing site for a French mental health startup.
longDescription: Reciproq is a French startup working to improve access to mental health care. Over a two-month engagement I built key pages of its first marketing site in Next.js and Tailwind, implementing the Figma design system with a mobile-first, accessible and performance-minded approach, plus data-driven modules for testimonials and pricing so the team could update content without a deploy.
